exposure: mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section after labor, scheduled cesarean section)
outcome: average number of breastfeeding sessions per day
average amount of time spent at each breastfeeding session
average number of newborn stools produced daily
average number of wet diapers produced daily
cohort: Nulliparous patients with term, singleton deliveries, excluding those with major postpartum complications, general anesthesia, or major fetal anomalies, at a large academic institution from 2017 to 2018.
finding: Women who deliver by cesarean section, regardless of the presence or absence of labor, are less likely to maintain exclusive breastfeeding postpartum and more likely to require formula supplementation.
mod_finding: Women who undergo cesarean delivery, whether scheduled or after labor, show decreased breastfeeding success, including increased need for formula supplementation and reduced frequency of breastfeeding sessions, compared to those with vaginal deliveries.
birth_weight: Babies from term, singleton deliveries (no specific weight range provided)
gest_age: Term deliveries (no specific gestational age range provided)
